defect.visual_evidence: Continuous bright solder joining two adjacent fine-pitch pads.

hypotheses.text: Stencil wear is increasing deposited solder volume, causing bridging between fine-pitch pads.
Reflow peak temperature drifted upward after work order WO-388 (profile change), causing excess solder flow and bridging.
Elevated room humidity is slowing flux activation, leading to solder bridging.
A shift change to operator OP-17 increased variability in manual touch-up, causing bridging.

D1.text: Team: Priya R. · Quality Engineer, Sree Electronics (fictional) (lead), the Line 2 SMT process engineer, and the reflow maintenance technician responsible for WO-388, formed in response to complaint C-2026-031 [Complaint C-2026-031].

D2.text: Hoshino Denso (fictional) reported solder bridging on product ECU-PCB-7, lot L2611, affecting 14 of 500 units shipped, with an 8D required within 10 working days [Complaint C-2026-031]. Vision inspection of the returned unit classified the defect as solder_bridge, severity major, at confidence 0.86 [Vision defect classification].

D3.text: Lots L2609, L2610, L2611, L2612, L2613 and L2614 from Line 2 are placed on hold pending disposition, covering the production window affected by WO-388's reflow profile change [Lot genealogy (WO-388 window)]. The hold will remain in place until reflow profile verification required under control plan item 6 is complete [Control plan item 6].

citations.label: Lot genealogy (WO-388 window)
citations.quote: Lots produced on Line 2 during the WO-388 out-of-profile window: L2609, L2610, L2611, L2612, L2613, L2614.

citations.label: Control plan item 6
citations.quote: Item 6 — Reflow profile verification after maintenance. Reflow peak temperature must be held within 235-250 °C per the qualified profile. Reaction plan: hold lots, re-profile.

D4.text: Root cause: reflow peak temperature on Line 2 drifted upward after profile change work order WO-388, pushing solder past liquidus for longer than specified and causing bridging between adjacent fine-pitch pads [PFMEA row 14]. This cause was verified with a Welch t-test comparing defect lots against good lots: p = 0.0000, effect +8.2 °C mean peak temperature in defect lots [H2 statistical test result]. The condition escaped detection because the post-change profile verification required after WO-388 was left in status profile_verification_pending and was never completed before production resumed [WO-388 maintenance record].

D5.text: Permanent corrective action: re-qualify the Line 2 reflow profile to bring peak temperature back within the 235-250 °C specification limit [Control plan item 6] and complete the profile verification step before resuming production [WO-388 maintenance record]. Work order WO-412 is raised to execute and sign off this re-qualification.
